subject: ACME - latency & throughput benchmarks
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@acme.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Apr 2026 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: ACME discovery — post-call recap + benchmarks

Hi Alex —

Great to meet today — thanks for taking the time to walk through your latency-sensitive use case. Quick recap and next steps from our call: 

- Goal: integrate low-latency text generation for customer-facing chat (target p95 under 200ms for 256-token responses).
- Current constraints: ~500 concurrent users during peak, preference for hosted API initially, potential move to Dedicated later.
- Action items for Redwood: share our measured latency/throughput benchmarks for similar models and a short summary of expected SLA behaviors.

I've attached a short benchmark summary (acme_latency_benchmarks_v1.pdf) — highlights:
- p50: ~40–60ms for short responses (<=64 tokens)
- p95: ~120–180ms depending on payload and batching (256 tokens case included)
- Throughput: up to ~75 req/s on a single reserved GPU under sustained small-batch load (numbers vary by model/config)

Next steps:
1) Jonas (cc'ed) will run one targeted run using the model profile we discussed and share the raw results.
2) If those look good, we can schedule a short proof-of-concept run in your staging environment.

Are you still aiming for an early-May decision on a pilot? If yes, I can coordinate a quick POC calendar block.

Thanks —
— Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0134
\Attachments: acme_latency_benchmarks_v1.pdf

From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Apr 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME discovery — post-call recap + benchmarks

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the recap. A couple of follow-ups from our infra/engineering side: 

- For the p95 numbers you shared, can you confirm token-count assumptions (e.g., 256 tokens includes prompt+response or response only)?
- What concurrency was used for the 75 req/s throughput figure? We need expected steady-state qps at ~500 concurrent users — is autoscaling the recommended approach or do you expect Dedicated reserved capacity?
- Any variance observed for function-calling / structured output workloads?

If you can send the raw run details (latency distributions and config for the run), that will help our infra team validate. Also copying procurement (procurement@acme.com) since we'll likely need costing for a pilot.
\Alex
Product Manager, Acme Corp

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, procurement@acme.com
Date: Thu, 23 Apr 2026 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME discovery — post-call recap + benchmarks

On Wed, Apr 22, 2026 at 10:12 AM Alex Chen <alex.chen@acme.com> wrote:
> For the p95 numbers you shared, can you confirm token-count assumptions (e.g., 256 tokens includes prompt+response or response only)?
> What concurrency was used for the 75 req/s throughput figure?
> Any variance observed for function-calling / structured output workloads?

Thanks for the questions — Jonas ran the detailed suite this morning and I attached the raw CSV + log. TL;DR answers below and a few notes on config: 

- Token assumptions: p95 numbers in the summary were reported for total tokens (prompt + response). The 256-token example assumes ~128 tokens prompt + 128 tokens response.
- Concurrency / throughput: the 75 req/s number was observed on a single reserved GPU with sustained small batching (batch size 4) at ~50% system utilization. For 500 concurrent active users we recommend either Dedicated with 2–3 reserved GPUs (depending on expected peak qps and response size) or hosted + autoscaling with burst capacity. Jonas can size more precisely after you share a target qps per user.
- Function-calling / structured outputs: we observed a modest latency increase (~10–20% p95) when enabling structured output and function-calling due to post-processing hooks. If you expect heavy function-calling, we'd include that in the POC run.

Attachments: acme_latency_throughput_results_20260423.csv, benchmark-run-20260423-aws-gpu.log

Next proposed step: Jonas and I can run one POC-configured workload against your staging endpoints (if you can provide a short-term test key / staging endpoint) or we can run a fully managed rehearsal on Redwood's staging environment and share results.

Let me know which you'd prefer and whether early-May still works for decisioning.

— Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
